newsitem.title: UK: UK's Offer confirms electricity opening to start April.
newsitem.headline: UK's Offer confirms electricity opening to start April.

text.p: British electricity regulator Stephen Littlechild said extending competition to all customers in the UK electricity market was his main aim and that he was committed to opening the market from next April.

"The timetable is extremely tight," he told a news conference. "A number of companies will be ready in April 1998, but a number of companies will not. Is it wise to delay the start of competition? My view is unambiguously not. We shouldn't be moving at the pace of the slowest, but at the pace of the fastest."

Littlechild said it should be possible to bring all companies into the competitive market "within a few months" of April 1998. He believes that all companies planning to enter the market will be ready by the end of July next year, and said that integrated testing was already under way.

He said in reply to a question that he did not believe it made sense to delay competition to July, given that perhaps only three companies would be ready by April and he believed all would be ready by July.

"It would send the wrong signals," he said, adding that some participants were already trying to speed up to be ready for the April deadline while others would be ready to compete between April and July.
He was concerned that full testing should be complete before competition started, especially to ensure that Information Technology systems were working.

"We are very concerned that customers should not just have access to competition but should not be disrupted," he said. "Customers are going to be choosing on the basis of quality of service as well as price."

Littlechild was speaking at the publication of the 1996 Annual Report of Offer, the Office of Electricity Regulation. He said that Offer was learning from the experience of the Office of Gas Supply, Ofgas, the gas industry regulator, especially in the area of marketing.

"Some tactics (practised by gas marketers in the run- up to market opening) were not acceptable and have now largely ceased. Electricity companies have taken note. We are working on a Code of Practice and hope to nip any problems in the bud."
